title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

standard_text: Functioning of a lens in the human eye, defects of vision and their corrections, applications of spherical mirrors and lenses. Refraction of light through a prism, dispersion of light, scattering of light, applications in daily life.

key_big: Myopia: concave lens. Hypermetropia: convex lens.
key_sub: Blue light scatters most; red least.
body_html:
How to think about it

The eye lens focuses images on the retina; ciliary muscles change its focal length (accommodation). The near point of a normal eye is about 25 cm and the far point is infinity. A myopic eye cannot see far objects (corrected by a concave lens); a hypermetropic eye cannot see near objects (corrected by a convex lens).

A prism disperses white light into seven colours (VIBGYOR) because each colour bends by a different amount. Atmospheric refraction makes stars twinkle and gives an early sunrise. Scattering by air molecules makes the sky blue and the rising and setting Sun red.

Example

Far point of a myopic eye is 2 m. Lens power?

f = −2 m

P = 1/f

Answer: −0.5 D

Example

Why is the sky blue?

air scatters short wavelengths most

Answer: blue light is scattered most

Common mistakes

  • Using a convex lens for myopia.
  • Saying red light scatters most.
  • Thinking planets twinkle like stars.

faq.a: The ability of the eye lens to change its focal length so that both near and far objects are seen clearly.

faq.q: Why does the Sun look red at sunset?
faq.a: Sunlight passes through more air, so blue light is scattered away and mostly red light reaches us.

items.q: Which part of the eye does this: fine-adjusting the focal length to focus images on the retina?
items.e: The eye lens: fine-adjusting the focal length to focus images on the retina.

items.q: Why do we see the Sun about 2 minutes before actual sunrise?
c: atmospheric refraction bends sunlight towards us
the Sun is closer in the morning
the Earth spins faster in the morning
items.e: Sunset is delayed by about 2 minutes too.

items.q: What is the job of the retina?

items.e: The optic nerve: carrying electrical signals from the retina to the brain.

items.q: Which colour bends the most in a prism?
items.e: Violet has the shortest wavelength; red bends the least.

items.q: Why does the sun look flattened (oval) near the horizon?

items.q: What did Newton show with a second, inverted prism?
